questions.q: What is the core shift as you move from Salesforce Data Analyst up to CRM Analytics Developer?
options: From answering one question at a time to building reusable assets that let others answer their own
From working with data to working only with user permissions
From using SQL to using no query language at all
From working alone to never speaking with stakeholders
questions.explain: The ladder's key transition is from answering questions to building the datasets and dashboards that enable many people to explore on their own.

questions.q: Which rung is described as moving Salesforce data into a warehouse, modeling it, and version-controlling that work?
options: Salesforce Data Analyst
Senior Salesforce Data Analyst
Salesforce Analytics Engineer
Salesforce Administrator
questions.explain: Analytics Engineers move and model data (for example in Snowflake with dbt, under Git), which goes beyond analyzing data inside Salesforce.

questions.q: How should you treat the salary ranges quoted in this lesson?
options: As guaranteed offers at every company
As directional only, since pay depends on city, company, industry, and the specific posting
As irrelevant because analyst pay never varies
As the exact base salary for every Senior role
questions.explain: Salary claims here are hedged: current postings suggest patterns, but you should always check postings in your own market.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what skills stay load-bearing at every rung of the ladder?
options: Only Tableau dashboard formatting
Only Salesforce administration
SQL, an understanding of the Salesforce data model, and clear communication
None; each rung starts over with entirely new skills
questions.explain: Higher rungs add layers above and beneath your foundation, but SQL, data model knowledge, and communication remain essential.

questions.q: Where does this capstone course sit in the path?
options: It teaches CRM Analytics and Snowflake from scratch
It closes the Job-Ready stage by applying existing tools on three projects and interview practice
It replaces the SQL and SOQL courses
It is a prerequisite for T-SQL
questions.explain: This course adds no new tools; it applies the earlier toolkit to projects and interview prep, and the advanced courses come afterward.
